reading.body:
All seven tools in this category generate slide decks from a text prompt or outline rather than assisting a human who is designing slides by hand, which is a different product category than traditional presentation software.

Most are US-based, Beautiful.ai, Decktopus, Gamma, Presentations.AI, and Tome, with one European entry, Pitch AI out of Germany, and one from India, SlidesAI. Decktopus is specifically flagged for data exposure risk, and Presentations.AI for content governance, which points to the same underlying concern from two angles, once a deck-generation tool has ingested a company's outline or source material to produce slides, that material has left the user's control in a way it would not have if a person built the deck manually in local software. Tome's note centers on narrative design and creative IP rather than data handling, suggesting its risk profile is more about who owns AI-generated creative output than about data exposure.

The data lists no URL for Tome, unlike every other tool in this set, which is worth noting as a gap rather than an omission with meaning. It does not say how these tools differ in output quality, pricing, or adoption, only what each is built to do and what data or IP question it raises.
